newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALY'S WORLD CUP SQUAD HIT BY INJURY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALY'S WORLD CUP SQUAD HIT BY INJURY.

text.p: Italian coach Arrigo Sacchi's World Cup campaign suffered a double blow on Sunday when injuries ruled Alessandro Del Piero and Demetrio Albertini out of his squad for qualifying matches against Moldavia and Georgia.
Del Piero pulled out after twisting a knee in the opening minute of Juventus's late night win over Fioretina while a calf muscle strain accounted for Albertini, Milan's main playmaker.
Sacchi has called up the uncapped Damiano Tommasi of Roma to reinforce his injury-hit midfield for the opening Group 2 qualifiers.

The 22-year-old Tommasi, a regular in the Under-21 side that won this year's European championships, caught the limelight after a series of versatile performances for Roma, the club he joined in the summer from Verona.
Gianluca Pessotto, Juventus's promising left-back is the only other newcomer to a squad built largely around the same players who suffered an humiliating first round elimination at Euro 96.
Italy are due to play away to Moldavia and at home to Georgia, on October 4 and 9 respectively, in their first outing since the Euro 96 debacle.
Also in the squad are Middlesborough's Fabrizio Ravanelli, top scorer in England's premier league, and Roberto Di Matteo of Chelsea.

As expected, there are recalls for two Juventus players: defender Ciro Ferrara and midfielder Antonio Conte, who both missed Euro 96 after sustaining injuries in their side's European Cup win over Ajax.

Squad: Luca Bucci, Francesco Toldo; Christian Panucci, Amedeo Carbone, Alessandro Costacurta, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Maldini, Alessandro Nesta, Gianluca Pessotto; Dino Baggio, Antonio Conte, Angelo Di Livio, Diego Fuser, Roberto Di Matteo, Damiano Tommasi; Pierluigi Casiraghi, Enrico Chiesa, Fabrizio Ravanelli, Gianfranco Zola.
